name: Federal Act on Data Protection (revised — nFADP)

articles.title: Processing principles
articles.requirement: Personal data processed lawfully, in good faith, and proportionately. Purpose specification; data minimisation; accuracy; integrity & confidentiality. Sensitive data + profiling triggers heightened safeguards.

articles.title: Privacy by design and by default
articles.requirement: Controllers implement appropriate technical and organisational measures from the design stage. Default settings restrict processing to what is strictly necessary for the purpose (data minimisation by default).

articles.title: Data security
articles.requirement: Appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised processing — confidentiality, integrity, availability, traceability. Federal Council ordinance (DPO) sets minimum standards.

articles.title: Records of processing activities
articles.requirement: Controllers and processors maintain a record of processing activities (purpose, categories, recipients, retention, TOMs, transfer countries). Simplified version for SMEs (< 250 employees and no high-risk processing). Production to FDPIC on request.

articles.title: International transfers — adequacy
articles.requirement: Transfer to a country with adequate protection (as listed by Federal Council). EU/EEA, UK, Andorra, Canada (commercial), etc. on the adequacy list. Otherwise transfer permitted only with safeguards under Art. 17.

articles.title: International transfers — safeguards
articles.requirement: Non-adequate countries: transfer allowed with (a) FDPIC-approved SCCs / IDTA-equivalent; (b) BCRs; (c) approved codes of conduct or certification; (d) approved contractual clauses. Specific exceptions: consent, performance of contract, public interest, vital interests, manifestly public data, legal claims.

articles.title: Right to information
articles.requirement: Data subjects informed of collection — identity of controller, processing purpose, categories of data, retention, recipients (especially in non-adequate countries), automated decisions with legal effect. Information provided actively at point of collection.

articles.title: Automated individual decisions
articles.requirement: Where a decision producing legal effect or substantially affecting the data subject is based solely on automated processing, the controller must inform the data subject + provide an opportunity to express their views + obtain human review. Exceptions: contract necessity (with safeguards), legal authorisation, consent.

articles.title: Data protection impact assessment (DPIA)
articles.requirement: DPIA mandatory where processing is likely to result in high risk to personality / fundamental rights: large-scale special-category data, systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas, evaluation / scoring including profiling, new technologies. Consultation of FDPIC where residual high risk remains.

articles.title: Breach notification
articles.requirement: Controllers notify the FDPIC of personal-data breaches likely to result in high risk to data subjects 'as soon as possible'. Notification covers: nature, contact details, likely consequences, mitigation measures. Data subjects notified when necessary for their protection.

articles.title: Right of access
articles.requirement: Data subjects entitled to free access to their personal data, including: data + categories, processing purpose, source where known, recipients, retention, automated-decision logic. Response within 30 days; extension possible with reasons. Restrictions for overriding interests, third-party rights, or manifestly excessive requests.

articles.title: Criminal sanctions
articles.requirement: Criminal sanction (against the responsible individual — not the company) up to CHF 250,000 for wilful breach of information / access / data security / cross-border-transfer / DPIA / professional-secrecy obligations. Prosecution is by cantonal authority on complaint by FDPIC or data subject.
